- If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.5) and forecast is trending downward, increase the forecast by 2–5% to account for bullish momentum.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ 0.0) and forecast is trending upward, reduce the forecast by 2–5% to account for bearish sentiment.  
- After a sharp price spike (true outcome > 80), model tends to overcorrect; reduce forecast by 3–8% in next 3–5 days to avoid overshoot.  
- If forecast is consistently below true outcome for 3+ consecutive days, apply a 1–3% upward bias to avoid underestimating mean reversion.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome exceeds forecast by >10% in first 5 days, assume momentum bias and adjust forecast upward by 1–3% per day until convergence.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.33–0.50 spikes, model tends to underreact; increase forecast by 1–3% to align with sentiment momentum.
